# BurgerAPI — LLM Reference (full)

BurgerAPI is a Bun-native API framework for building APIs and web apps. It uses file-based routing, a hybrid router (Bun-native for static paths, a trie for dynamic/wildcard), a shared request context (`BurgerContext`), Zod validation, middleware, and automatic OpenAPI 3.0 generation with Swagger UI. Current version: 0.11.0.

This file is a complete reference for AI coding tools. Code samples use the current API.

================================================================
## Install & run
================================================================
```
bun add burger-api
```
```ts
// src/index.ts
import { Burger } from "burger-api";

const burger = new Burger({ apiDir: "api" });
burger.serve(4000);
```

Routes live in `route.ts` files under `apiDir`. Each file exports functions named after HTTP methods:
```ts
// api/hello/route.ts
import type { BurgerRequest } from "burger-api";

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  return Response.json({ message: "Hello world" });
}
```

================================================================
## Architecture
================================================================
A request flows through a single pipeline:
Incoming Request → Bun Native Router → Hybrid Router → BurgerContext → Middleware → Validation → Handler → Response Processing → Response.

- Hybrid Router: static paths via Bun's native router; dynamic (`:param`) and wildcard (`*`) via a trie; priority static > dynamic > wildcard.
- BurgerContext: one lightweight request context object per request, built from a shared prototype. Fields are lazy getters, so unused data (e.g. query) is never parsed or allocated.
- Response Processing: `req.set` mutations are merged once at the pipeline exit by `applySet`; the original `Response` is returned unchanged when nothing is set.

================================================================
## BurgerRequest (the `req` object)
================================================================
`BurgerRequest` extends the standard `Request`. It adds:

- `req.params: Record<string, string> | undefined`
  Dynamic path parameters. For `/users/[id]`, `req.params.id` is the value. Undefined for routes without params.

- `req.query: Record<string, string | string[]> | undefined`
  The parsed query string, evaluated lazily on first read. Repeated keys become arrays. Prefer this over `new URL(req.url)` because it parses only when used and avoids allocating a `URL` object. `+` is decoded to space, matching `URLSearchParams` semantics.

- `req.route: { path: string; pattern: string } | undefined`
  The matched route. `path` is the requested pathname (no query string); `pattern` is the route definition pattern (e.g. `/users/:id`, `/files/*`). Present on EVERY matched route, including static routes served through Bun's native router.

- `req.validated: { params?; query?; body? }`
  Data validated by the route's Zod schemas. Typed from the schema. Undefined fields when no schema is declared for that target.

- `req.set: { status?: number; headers?: Record<string, string> | Headers } | undefined`
  Response mutation intent. Applied at the pipeline exit by `applySet`.

- `req.wildcardParams: string[] | undefined`
  Catch-all segments for `[...slug]` routes.

Inherited from `Request`: `method`, `url`, `headers`, `signal`, `body`, `bodyUsed`, `json()`, `text()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `blob()`, `formData()`, `clone()`.

================================================================
## Request API examples
================================================================
```ts
// Dynamic param
export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const { id } = req.params;
  return Response.json({ id });
}

// Query (lazy)
export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const { limit = "10", tag } = req.query;
  return Response.json({ limit, tag });
}

// Route metadata
export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  // req.route.pattern === "/users/:id"
  return Response.json({ pattern: req.route.pattern });
}

// Validated data
export const schema = {
  get: { query: z.object({ limit: z.coerce.number().optional() }) },
};
export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const { limit } = req.validated.query; // typed + validated
  return Response.json({ limit });
}
```

================================================================
## Response mutation (req.set)
================================================================
```ts
export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  req.set = {
    status: 201,
    headers: { "x-total": "42" },
  };
  return Response.json({ created: true });
}
```
- `req.set.status` overrides the response status only when defined.
- `req.set.headers` is merged over existing headers; explicit values win.
- `applySet` runs once at the pipeline exit, uniformly on GET and auto-HEAD responses. When `req.set` is empty, the original `Response` is returned without rebuild.

================================================================
## Routing
================================================================
- Static: `api/health/route.ts` → `GET /api/health`
- Dynamic: `api/users/[id]/route.ts` → `GET /api/users/:id`, read `req.params.id`
- Wildcard: `api/files/[...]/route.ts` → `GET /api/files/*`, read `req.wildcardParams`
- Nested: `api/blog/[id]/comments/route.ts` → `/api/blog/:id/comments`
- Route groups: `(admin)/dashboard/route.ts` → `/api/admin/dashboard` (the group folder does not appear in the URL)
- API prefix: `apiPrefix` option (default `api`).
- Static pages: `.tsx`/`.html` files under the page directory.

================================================================
## Middleware
================================================================
```ts
import type { BurgerRequest, Middleware } from "burger-api";

const requireAuth: Middleware = (req) => {
  const auth = req.headers.get("authorization");
  if (!auth?.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
    return Response.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, { status: 401 });
  }
  return undefined; // continue
};

export const middleware = [requireAuth];

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```
Return types:
- `Response` — stop and send it.
- `function (response) => Response` — transform the final response after the handler (after-middlewares run in reverse order).
- `undefined` — continue.

Global middleware: pass `globalMiddleware` to the `Burger` constructor.

================================================================
## Validation
================================================================
```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const schema = {
  get: {
    query: z.object({ limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).optional() }),
  },
  post: {
    body: z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), price: z.number().positive() }),
  },
};

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const { limit } = req.validated.query;
  return Response.json({ limit });
}
```
Validation targets: `params`, `query`, `body`. Invalid requests receive a structured error (HTTP 400) before the handler runs. See docs for the error shape.

================================================================
## OpenAPI & Swagger UI
================================================================
OpenAPI 3.0 is generated from routes and Zod schemas. Add route metadata via an `openapi` export:
```ts
export const openapi = {
  get: { summary: "List products", tags: ["products"], operationId: "listProducts" },
};
```
Swagger UI is served automatically.

================================================================
## Examples
================================================================
CRUD API (list with pagination + response headers, read one, create):
```ts
// api/products/route.ts
export const schema = {
  get: { query: z.object({ limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(10) }) },
  post: { body: z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), price: z.number().positive() }) },
};

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const { limit } = req.validated.query;
  req.set = { headers: { "x-total": String(products.length) } };
  return Response.json(products.slice(0, limit));
}

export async function POST(req: BurgerRequest) {
  const body = await req.json();
  const product = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), ...body };
  products.push(product);
  req.set = { status: 201 };
  return Response.json(product);
}
```
Authentication: see the bearer-token middleware example above. Pagination: read `req.query.page`/`req.query.limit`, set `x-total`/`x-page` via `req.set`.

Full example apps: Todo API and Blog API (tutorials), plus CRUD, Authentication, and Pagination examples in the docs.

================================================================
## Server options (Burger constructor)
================================================================
- `apiDir: string` — directory of API route files. Required unless `apiRoutes` is set.
- `apiPrefix: string` — prefix for API routes (default `api`).
- `pageDir: string` — directory of static page files.
- `pagePrefix: string` — prefix for pages (default `pages`).
- `globalMiddleware: Middleware[]` — middleware for every request.
- `title`, `description`, `version` — OpenAPI metadata.
- `debug: boolean` — extra logging.
- `apiRoutes`, `pageRoutes` — pre-built routes for production builds (no runtime filesystem scan).

================================================================
## CLI
================================================================
- `burger-api create <name>` — scaffold a project.
- `burger-api add <middleware>` — add an ecosystem middleware.
- `burger-api serve` — run the dev server.
- `burger-api build <entry>` — bundle for production.
- `burger-api build:exec <entry>` — build a standalone executable.

================================================================
## Ecosystem
================================================================
Bundled middleware: CORS, Logger, Rate Limiter, JWT Auth, API Key Auth, and more. Add via the CLI.
